headline: Joint multi-view models integrate heterogeneous biomedical data for prediction
label: Multimodal Biomedical Data Integration
summary: Recent papers pair relational structure with multi-omics, drug, and natural-product inputs to make predictions traceable and interpretable.
synthesis: The common thread is relational or multi-view structure imposed on heterogeneous biomedical inputs. GONet fuses mRNA, miRNA, and protein profiles over molecular interaction networks for cancer subtype and stage classification. SADRP encodes drug structure through shortest-path and edge encodings alongside cell-line gene expression and methylation to predict drug response. UCEC applies a knowledge graph with uncertainty-calibrated evidence chains to prioritize natural product-disease associations with traceable mechanisms. MV-S2M models circRNA-miRNA interactions in a multi-view state-space framework with structure-aware diffusion and disease-mediated subgraphs, enabling zero-shot prediction. The imbalance-aware BioBERT drug-food interaction classifier is a distinct, text-based case, using class weighting and focal loss to handle skewed safe, neutral, and unsafe labels. The thread is dominant but not universal; the novelty lies in joint modelling of multiple views, with graph scaffolds where used.
